stops.note: usually explained as 'of the wilderness', from ilang; the tree (Cananga odorata) is native to the Philippines and Indonesia
entered English through the perfume trade; French colonial planters in the 1900s made the Comoros and Madagascar's Nosy Be the main producers, and Chanel No. 5 (1921) uses its oil
stops.meaning: perfume oil from the cananga flower

current_meaning: a tropical tree with fragrant yellow flowers; the perfume oil made from them
